cold_open.title: The Lantern Tax
beats: Last night a goblin clerk knocked on my crypt with an invoice for the lanterns.
Every lantern in the Ninth Dark, he said, owes the Guild a copper a flicker.
I asked him who set the price. He pointed at a ledger older than my phylactery.
So I read the ledger. Page one: the Guild owes me rent for the darkness between lanterns.
The clerk did the sums, went pale, and offered to pay in goblins.
I accepted. That is why the new minions smell faintly of lamp oil.
cold_open.handoff: Now then, my lamp-oil recruits: who among you has come to pay tribute tonight?

lines: Name one thing you would hide in my moat, and I will rule whether it drowns or rules the moat.
bits.payoff: Crown the best answer Moat Regent for the night.

lines: Confess the pettiest grudge you hold, and I will judge it worthy of the Ledger or the bin.
bits.payoff: Enter the pettiest grudge in the Ledger with full ceremony.

lines: Pitch me a villain plan in five words or fewer; the weakest pitch cleans the throne.
bits.payoff: Sentence the weakest pitch to throne-polishing duty.

lines: Before I was a lich, I tried a career in haunted real estate.
My first listing was a castle with three ghosts and no plumbing, and I described it as rustic.
The ghosts sued me for calling them rustic, and they won.
Which is why, to this day, I pay three ghosts a pension in cold soup.
bits.payoff: He still pays the ghosts; the soup is the joke.

lines: The Bureau of Lost Socks would like a word, minions.

connectors.line: Enough of the clerk. The room is full; let us begin.
Now, while you minions think of something clever, a matter for the court.
But enough about me. Well, never enough. Back to you lot.
Decisions, decisions: the court will vote.
The night turns; another chamber calls.
